## This documentation build {#sec-build-status}

Source revision: **{{< var build.sha >}}**. Full commit identifier:
`{{< var build.commit >}}`. Rendered **{{< var build.rendered >}}**.

This book publishes the source snapshot and supplied measurements, not a new
execution of the science suite. A modified working tree is labeled in the
revision. [Test evidence](test-results.qmd) carries its own source fingerprint
and scope; [performance](performance.qmd) separates kernel from full-run timings.

## What is and is not certified {#sec-certification-status}

| Claim | Evidence required |
|---|---|
| Documentation integrity | Successful render, source provenance checks, local link/fragment check |
| Current extraction CPU tests | Current `scripts/validate.jl --backend=cpu` record and log |
| Metal/CUDA hardware correctness | Separate successful record on that device, with documented coverage |
| A physical recombination or PMF conclusion | Matched temporal/spatial/spectral/start-redshift/chemistry convergence artifacts |
| Full Boltzmann or nonlinear Lyman-alpha accuracy | Not established by the current P1/smoothing/response-table model |
| Reproduction of all Schiff 3D results | Not claimed by shipping linear reference tools or example configurations |

Historical upstream Metal gates and performance figures are **not current
extraction certification**. Source support for CUDA is **not CUDA hardware
validation**. A `NOT_RUN` device stays unmeasured even if another backend passes.

## Source lineage {#sec-lineage}

- MHD and Poisson sources were extracted from Vespa's `lib/MHDKernels` and
  `lib/PoissonKernels`; the full runner descends from
  `MHDKernels/test/pmf_dm_lattice_bench.jl`.
- Chemistry and emission are bundled from `ChemistryKernels.jl` and
  `EmissionKernels.jl`, preserving their source and license notices.
- Portable Schiff/LMHD, photon, and Lyman-alpha reference/analysis algorithms
  descend from `vespa-runs/tools/sv25_reference`. Their own provenance lists
  copied source hashes and adaptations, including dirty-working-tree content.
- This book adapts the actual [Quadrant template](https://github.com/yipihey/quadrant):
  its Quarto book structure, brand palette, theme-aware tokens, source/test
  provenance conventions, numbered math, notation/status appendices, and footer.
  Rustdoc resolution was replaced by checked local Julia source snapshots;
  there is no WebAssembly simulator or fabricated laboratory.

The machine-readable extraction record is `provenance/extraction.json`;
the independent science tools use `tools/reference/provenance.json`. Subsequent
standalone fixes can intentionally differ from the initially recorded imported
hashes. Use the run's `source_fingerprint_sha256` for its actual implementation.

## Licensing and credit {#sec-attribution}

The integration, extracted project-owned numerical/reference code, and
documentation are distributed under the root BSD-3-Clause license, with
`CITATION.cff` providing the software citation. Retain per-component notices.
Chemistry/Emission retain their
University of Illinois/NCSA-style Enzo license text. Do not infer that those
licenses automatically cover external manuscripts, datasets, or software.
The extraction provenance records the source state; the root license supplies
this distribution's terms for the project-owned reference implementation.

Credit the original scientific algorithms, source projects, reference models,
and the specific numerical/physics modifications used for a result. Cite
Schiff/Venumadhav or Jedamzik/Abel work only for the model actually compared;
the package's examples are not a replacement for reading the original papers.
No paper acceptance, DOI, or historical campaign certification is asserted here.

## How to cite and share {#sec-cite}

The repository's `CITATION.cff` supplies citation metadata without inventing a
software DOI. Cite **PMFGLM.jl, Tom Abel and contributors**, the
[repository](https://github.com/yipihey/pmf-glm), the exact commit or source
fingerprint, and the numerical model/settings used. Include reference-tool
provenance for oracle-based comparisons. Do not cite an uncommitted working tree
as if it were an immutable release.

Share configurations, resolved environments, raw tables, test records, logs,
and scripts with figures. Hypothesis annotations are available for discussion;
GitHub issues and edit/source links support corrections. Avoid publishing
machine-local paths, private data, or huge checkpoints without review.
